A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research, renamed from Energy-Driven Steering (EDS) to Energy Landscape Steering (ELS). Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, inference timing, multi-turn robustness tests and ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds an SFT comparison, architecture and layer-selection ablations, alternative-training results and paired model-output examples.

M1.justification: The three-phase procedure, external MLP energy models, InfoNCE objective, gradient-based activation steering and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. EDS becomes ELS; the simpler architecture is an ablation, and the expanded classifier description documents implementation.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 and Table 7 add training on WildJailBreak using 1,000 benign and 1,000 harmful prompts. The original CARES/SafeMedEval medical training condition and evaluation task coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a standalone SFT comparator alongside the retained Defender-Only and Self-Play variants. Surgical Vector/Vector Ablation becomes Surgical; CAST, AdaSteer and AlphaSteer were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Existing configurations and evaluation settings in Tables 4–5 remain unchanged. New Table 6 introduces three-layer versus four-layer EBM controls, top-5/10/15/20 layer selections and early/middle/late intervention conditions.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens supplementary analysis through architecture and layer-region ablations, alternative training-domain evaluation and three paired rollout case studies testing refusal correction, safety and coherence. The original hyperparameter sweeps are retained as Appendix D.1/Figure 5, and existing robustness and decision-boundary analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. New results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive results for SFT, architecture/layer choices, alternative training and paired outputs. Table 6 reports ORB-H compliance of 78.4% versus 82.6% for the simpler and original EBMs. Table 7 reports WildJailBreak-trained ELS at 83.7% ORB-H and 66.7% MMLU. Existing main results remain unchanged; Table 7 represents a different training condition, not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix C becomes v2 Appendix E, retaining the definitions, lemma, theorem, corollary and derivations in Equations 13–44. The added intuitive overview and equation reformatting introduce no substantive theoretical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that an external EBM enables inference-time reduction of false refusals while preserving safety and general capabilities. The abstract retains the same ORB-H example, 57.3% to 82.6%; renaming and additional evidence do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands applicability qualifications: fixed-data EBMs cannot adapt online, response-level labels miss partial refusals, and reasoning-model extensions remain future work. Appendix D.2 adds interpretations concerning normalization, dropout and middle-layer representations, while Appendix G interprets the new coherence examples.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly identifies the training classifier as refusal-substring matching following JailbreakBench. New experiments document the simpler EBM, layer controls and WildJailBreak source and sampling. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, execution instructions and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for already-tested CAST (Lee et al., 2024), AdaSteer (Zhao et al., 2025) and AlphaSteer (Sheng et al., 2025). It removes Azar et al. (2024) and Safe Unlearning (Zhang et al., 2024), while preserving the main research positioning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and EDS becomes ELS throughout much of the text. The abstract, related work and conclusion are edited, an intuitive theory overview is added, and hyperparameter ablations move to Appendix D.1. Most existing exposition and main-section order remain.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1, resizes and relocates existing displays, restyles prompt boxes and adds Tables 6–7 and boxed rollout examples. The original ablation and decision-boundary figures are retained with changed placement and numbering.

improvement.justification: The added controls, training-domain experiment and explicit limitations make the method easier to assess. These gains are limited by inaccurate interpretation: Appendix D.2 calls safety identical despite Table 6 showing JBB rates of 11.0% and 10.0%, and the capability-preservation claim is not qualified for Table 7's MMLU decline from the baseline's 68.1% to 66.7%.
